name: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) for well-log correlation: classic DTW and constrained variants (Sakoe-Chiba band, slope/stretch limits, stratigraphic tie constraints, local/subsequence DTW)
authors_org: Lineage: Sakoe & Chiba (1978, speech); Zoraster et al. (SPE 90471, 2004, first DP curve alignment for well-to-well logs); Hladil et al. (2010, DTW for log correlation, cited by Chevron US11180981); Sylvester (Basin Research 2023, DTW + relative geologic time multi-well); Samant et al. (Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology 2025, stratigraphic constraints in DTW); Align app (GSA Today, Feb 2024). In-competition: ROGII 3rd-place Local-DTW HMM ensemble member.
year: 1978 (algorithm); 2004 (first SPE well-log DP alignment); 2023-2025 (constrained and multi-well variants); 2025/2026 (ROGII 3rd-place local DTW)
venue_link: SPE ATCE 2004 https://onepetro.org/SPEATCE/proceedings/04ATCE/All-04ATCE/SPE-90471-MS/71708 ; Sylvester 2023 https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/bre.12787 ; Samant 2025 https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2024PA005082 ; Align (GSA Today 2024) https://www.geosociety.org/gsa-today/february-2024/align-a-userfriendly-app-for-numerical-stratigraphic-correlation ; Semi-automatic DTW log correlation (2023) https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374950910 ; ROGII 3rd-place writeup (local copy Erudition/3rd.txt)
code_availability: Generic DTW is widely available (dtaidistance, tslearn, pyts with Sakoe-Chiba/Itakura windows, dtw-python with step patterns and open-begin/open-end). Sylvester 2023 reportedly released Python code for DTW+RGT correlation [uncertain]. The ROGII 3rd-place Local-DTW HMM is part of the pipeline behind Erudition/rogii_exp417_gnll_five_groupkfold_submit.py (blended at weight 0.20).
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed for classic/constrained DTW on vertical logs and sedimentary sections; competition writeup (ROGII 3rd place) for local DTW on this exact task; search-snippet only for the 2025 Samant details (full text returned 403).
extreme_summary: DTW finds the minimum-cost monotone stretch/squeeze alignment between two logs by dynamic programming, with bands, slope limits and tie points keeping it geologically plausible. Plain DTW assumes a monotone depth-to-depth mapping, which breaks on laterals that go up and down through strata, so on our task it only works locally or after being recast as a lateral-sample to typewell-level DP (the Chevron patent and 2nd-place designs).
task_definition: Classic: given two vertical logs (reference/typewell and target), find a monotone warping path mapping each depth in one to a depth in the other, giving correlated tops. Geosteering adaptation: map each lateral MD sample to a typewell TVT position; plain DTW is valid only on stretches where the bit moves steadily up- or down-section.
inputs: GR (or other logs) of both wells; optional tie points/tops (user picks, cf. US11906683 'DTW of signals plus user picks'), sedimentation-rate bounds, age constraints (Samant 2025). For laterals: lateral GR vs typewell GR, optionally trajectory Z.
target_parameterisation: Warping path (index pairs i to j), i.e. a monotone depth-shift function; for a monotone lateral segment, a TVT(MD) curve.
output_representation: Single optimal path (argmin); soft-DTW gives a smoothed expected alignment matrix. No native calibrated uncertainty.
architecture: Non-learned DP over a cost matrix C[i,j] = |a(i) - b(j)| after normalization (z-score or histogram matching). Accumulated cost D[i,j] = C[i,j] + min(D[i-1,j], D[i,j-1], D[i-1,j-1]) with step patterns/weights, then backtrack. Variants: Sakoe-Chiba band |i-j| <= w; Itakura parallelogram; slope constraints (max consecutive horizontal/vertical moves = max stretch ratio); open-begin/open-end subsequence DTW (match a short lateral window anywhere in the typewell); derivative DTW; multi-log vector costs; amercing penalty per warping step (Herrmann & Webb 2021); soft-DTW (Cuturi & Blondel 2017) for differentiable use.
core_mechanism: Global optimal alignment under monotonicity: repeated/self-similar beds are disambiguated by ordering (bed A must precede bed B) plus stretch limits. On laterals this ordering constraint disappears because the bit can re-enter the same bed, which is exactly why band confusion is the dominant error in our task.
training_objective: None (classical). Differentiable relatives (soft-DTW, Drop-DTW) can serve as structured training losses; see item B05.
decoding: Min-cost path via backtracking (Viterbi-like hard argmin). Soft-DTW gives a temperature-controlled expected alignment.
metric_consistent_decode: Mode-seeking (argmin path), not Bayes-optimal for RMSE. The 2nd-place writeup and our own continuity decode (posterior_fb_decode.py) both found mode/continuity paths worse than the expectation.
evidence_scope: Whole log pair (global DTW) or a local window (subsequence/local DTW).
prefix_conditioning: Via fixed start point / tie points: the last known heel TVT can anchor an open-end DTW.
propose_vs_select: Single output per run; candidates can come from several band widths/windows or k-best paths. Usable as an ensemble member: 3rd place used a Local-DTW HMM at weight 0.20 purely for error diversity.
physical_constraints: Monotonicity (layer ordering), bounded stretch/squeeze (thickness-ratio limits), optional tie points and rate bounds. Monotonicity is correct vertically but wrong for undulating laterals.
dataset: Classic papers: pairs/sets of vertical wells (Zoraster 2004 field logs; Sylvester 2023 multi-well sets; Samant 2025 sediment cores/proxy records). ROGII 3rd place: Kaggle ROGII lateral + typewell data.
synthetic_to_real: Not applicable (no training). Normalization between logs is critical: std normalization (as in US11180981) or percentile/histogram matching.
metric_and_performance: Classic papers report qualitative correlation quality or tie errors, no lateral RMSE. ROGII 3rd place: adding the Local-DTW HMM family improved HMM-mixture OOF RMSE 6.0492 -> 5.9703 and combined HMMPF 5.6648 -> 5.6155, though it was not the strongest standalone model.
comparability: Only the 3rd-place number is on comparable data, and it is OOF CV inside an HMM/PF pipeline at about 5.6 ft, not our 155-well holdout. Our single model is 4.84 ft; the DTW-driven gain (~0.05 ft) is far below our +-0.39 ft single-run noise floor.
validation_protocol: Classic DTW: unsupervised, no held-out protocol. 3rd place: group K-fold OOF; their CV 5.29 vs private 5.84 gap warns about fitting blend weights on OOF.
inference_budget: O(N*M) per pair, O(N*w) with a band; milliseconds on CPU for a 345-column x 400-level grid. Negligible next to the CNN.
repeated_layers: Handled only through ordering and stretch limits. On laterals repeated patterns are re-crossings of the same bed plus self-similar beds at other levels; monotone DTW cannot represent re-crossing and forces a wrong ordering. Local/subsequence DTW handles re-crossings by matching windows independently, but then loses the global tie-breaker and becomes just a local matching cost, like our gr_abs_diff channels.
drift: Not addressed; DTW has no dip state. A slow systematic offset is absorbed as a warping shift unless rate constraints are added. The Chevron patent adds a pathbias term toward the survey trajectory for this reason.
uncertainty_and_calibration: None natively. Soft-DTW or forward-backward over the same lattice gives an alignment posterior, but it is uncalibrated.
where_to_use: (1) As an extra cost channel in the 16-channel input image: a windowed subsequence/derivative-DTW matching cost per (MD column, TVT level) that tolerates local bed thickening/thinning between the typewell and the lateral location, which a pointwise |GR - typewell GR| channel does not. (2) As a cheap, low-correlation blend member (as in 3rd place). Not as a decoder over our posterior.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%) via a stretch-tolerant matching cost; secondarily broad humps (~13%) where thickness change smears the pointwise cost. Does not target drift.
gap_vs_our_implementation: We have no stretch-tolerant (warped) matching cost: the cost image is pointwise GR difference per TVT hypothesis, and any tolerance to thickness change must be learned by the ConvNeXt receptive field. Neither the 1st-place nor the 2nd-place inputs explicitly model local bed-thickness change between typewell and lateral. We also have no DTW-family blend member (3rd place did). A global DTW-style decoder over our posterior is effectively covered already by the 2nd-place DP and the failed continuity forward-backward decode, so the remaining gap is on the evidence/input side.
proposed_experiment: A03-2 first (cheap diversity check): implement a standalone local-DTW tracker (lateral GR windows vs typewell, anchored at the last known TVT, open-end, Sakoe-Chiba band allowing +-20% thickness change), numba, script next to posterior_fb_decode.py in kaggle_1st_place/solution. Report its holdout RMSE on the 155 wells and its error correlation with ConvNeXt/FastViT predictions (results/cnx_mobileone_ep150). Keep only if correlation < ~0.7 and a FIXED-weight blend chosen on training OOF improves holdout by > 0.39 ft (no learned gates, which already failed). A03-1 (input channel): in the cost-image builder that produces the gr_abs_diff channels, add 1-2 channels: for each (MD column c, TVT level l), the subsequence-DTW cost between the lateral GR window [c-W, c+W] (W 3-5 columns, projected to TVT via trajectory Z under hypothesis l at c) and the typewell GR around l, normalized per well; precompute and cache under data/. Train ConvNeXt 60 ep with 17-18 channels vs the identical 16-channel control and seed; require > 0.39 ft gain, then confirm with a second seed and the 150-ep recipe before distilling to FastViT.
implementation_effort: Low for A03-2 (standalone tracker, ~200 lines numba). Medium for A03-1 (feature pipeline change, recache, retrain; TVT-hypothesis projection must match existing channels).
gpu_cost: Feature precompute is CPU-only (minutes with numba). A03-1 needs one 60-epoch ConvNeXt run on the RTX 5060 8 GB, same cost as the baseline; inference unchanged apart from 1-2 more input channels. A03-2 is CPU-only.
distillation_compatibility: Yes. An extra input channel is transparent to FastViT KD on output posteriors (the student gets the same channel). A standalone tracker is not distilled but can be a blend member.
error_correlation_with_ours: Standalone tracker: likely low correlation (different evidence usage, no learned prior) but much weaker, plausibly 7-10 ft [uncertain]; 3rd place observed low correlation with their base HMM. For the input-channel variant correlation is not the relevant question.
risk: (1) The ConvNeXt may already learn stretch-tolerant matching from the 16-channel image, making the channel redundant. (2) Weak standalone members rarely help a 4.8 ft model, learned gates already failed here, and the 3rd-place gain was ~0.05 ft at 5.6 ft, below our noise floor. (3) DTW is mode-seeking and monotone while laterals are non-monotone in TVT, so any global DTW decode repeats the failed continuity-decode result. (4) GR normalization mismatch between lateral and typewell can dominate the DTW cost.
notes: Main takeaway: DTW's disambiguating power in vertical correlation comes from the ordering constraint, and that is exactly what vanishes on undulating laterals. This is why Chevron (US11180981, which cites Hladil 2010 DTW) and the 2nd place recast alignment as a DP over (lateral sample, typewell level) with a move penalty. Related prior art: Zoraster 2004 (automated, interactive, constrained DP alignment); US11906683 (DTW plus user picks); US10853893 / US11704748 (automatic correlation of geologic tops). The Saudi horizontal-well correlation SPE papers (2013, 2021) update structure while geosteering but are probably not DTW-based [uncertain].
